label: SIMULATED OUTPUT — prepared in advance by the course team. Not generated live.
locale_note: All prepared English is British English (en-GB). Replay serves the same text whichever English variant the project uses.

translations.text: Start Investigation

Before Mid-Autumn, Osmanthus Street is hung full of lanterns. {player_name} just arrived at the street entrance and heard that the treasure of the lantern fair — the giant rabbit lantern — has flown away without wings.

You are the detective who came to investigate the case? Good, good. That rabbit lantern was tied by my own hands, one bamboo one paper, and it accompanied the neighbours for forty Mid-Autumns. The thief who stole the lantern, I think, is a rabbit's tail — cannot be long!
Grandma, calm down! That rabbit is bigger than my car, who can steal it? Unless it escaped by itself and ran back to the moon to find Sister Chang'e to celebrate Mid-Autumn.
Follow the colourful paper pieces on the ground
Go to the tea restaurant to ask the boss

The colourful paper pieces led all the way to the rooftop: the rabbit lantern sat there well, and the broken ear was patched with new paper. It turned out Ah Kit secretly moved it to repair, wanting to give Grandma a surprise.

The tea restaurant boss said while wiping the cup: 「Rabbit? Just sat on Ah Kit's motorcycle and left, still wearing a helmet.」 You rushed out the door, only saw a rabbit head floating farther and farther in the traffic……
Begin investigation
translations.note: Literal rendering of 開始調查.

translations.text: Are you the detective who has come to investigate the case? Good, good. translations.text: Ah Kit boy, late again! Said good to deliver mooncakes at seven, now it is already seven thirty. Being a person needs "one promise, a thousand gold", understand or not?
Grandma, I am wronged! Tonight all orders were full, I drove so fast I almost flew to the moon. Not one double yolk lotus seed paste was crushed, you should praise me!
Hmph, your mouth is faster than your car. Your generation, all day lowering heads to "clock in", cannot even tie one lantern, really each generation is not as good as the previous generation.
If cannot then learn. Grandma you teach me — your lantern although very old school, but really has feel, I am serious.
Please Grandma teach Ah Kit to tie lanterns
Let Ah Kit go to deliver the takeaway first

Grandma scolded Ah Kit "clumsy hands and clumsy feet" with her mouth, but her hands never stopped, teaching him one bamboo strip by one bamboo strip to tie rabbit ears. At midnight, there was one more crooked-head small rabbit lantern on the table.

Ah Kit jumped on the motorcycle, turned back and shouted: 「Grandma, tomorrow I help you carry the lantern, free!」 Grandma waved her hand: 「Go go, slow on the road, don't learn that rabbit to run around.」

Kit, you are late again! We agreed that you would deliver the mooncakes at seven o'clock, and now it is already half past seven. A person must keep a promise worth a thousand pieces of gold. Do you understand?
translations.note: 一諾千金 translated closely.

translations.text: Granny, I have been wronged! Every order tonight was full, and I rode so fast that I almost flew up to the moon. Not a single double-yolk lotus-paste mooncake was crushed. You should be praising me!

Hmph. Your mouth is even faster than your motorbike. Your generation lowers their heads all day to "check in", yet none of you can even make a single lantern. Truly, each generation is worse than the one before.
translations.note: 打卡 read as social-media check-ins.

translations.text: If I cannot do it, then I will learn. Granny, please teach me. Your lanterns are very old school, but they really have feel. I am serious.
translations.note: Kept the English words from the source.

translations.text: Ask Granny to teach Kit to make lanterns
translations.note: Exactly 40 characters.

translations.text: Let Kit finish his deliveries first

Granny scolded Kit aloud as "clumsy of hand and foot", but her hands never stopped, and strip by strip she taught him to make a rabbit's ear. At midnight, there was an extra small rabbit lantern with a tilted head on the table.

Kit jumped onto his motorbike, turned his head back and shouted, "Granny, tomorrow I will help you carry the lantern, free of charge!" Granny waved her hand. "Go, go. Be slow on the road, and do not run around like that rabbit."
Kit, late again! You said you'd bring the mooncakes at seven, and it's already half past. A promise is a promise, you know. Understand?

Granny, I've been framed! Orders were through the roof tonight, I was riding so fast I nearly flew to the moon. And not a single double-yolk lotus-paste mooncake got squashed. You ought to be praising me!
translations.note: 冤枉 as a mock-dramatic protest.

translations.text: Hmph. Your mouth's faster than your bike. Your lot spend all day staring at your phones, clocking in everywhere, and not one of you can make a single lantern. Every generation's worse than the last.
Then I'll learn, won't I? Teach me, Granny. Your lanterns are dead old school, but they've got real vibes. I mean it.
translations.note: 'Dead' and 'vibes' keep Kit young and British.

translations.text: Ask Granny to teach Kit her craft
Let Kit get back to his deliveries

Granny grumbles that Kit has two left hands, but hers never stop moving as she shows him, strip by strip, how to shape a rabbit's ear. By midnight there is a small new rabbit lantern on the table, head cocked to one side.

Kit jumps on his motorbike and shouts back, "Granny, I'll carry your lantern tomorrow, for free!" Granny waves him away. "Go on, go on. Take it slowly on the road, and don't go running off like that rabbit."
Kit, my lad! Late again! Seven o'clock, you swore, and the clock says half past. My word is my bond, young man, and so is yours. Or are those ears just for decoration?
translations.note: Granny's scolding made sharper and more affectionate.

translations.text: Granny, I'm innocent, I swear! Orders were off the scale tonight, I was going so fast I nearly hit orbit. Houston, we have mooncakes! And not one double-yolk got squished. Hero, me. Say it.
translations.note: A space joke for the moon exaggeration.

translations.text: Hmph. That mouth runs faster than your bike. You lot have your noses glued to your phones, "checking in" at every noodle stall, and not one of you can tie a lantern. Each generation is a sorrier sight than the last.
Can't do it? So I'll learn, easy. Go on, Granny, teach me! Your lanterns are well old school, yeah, but they've got proper heart. No lie.
translations.note: Code-mixing shown through teen slang.

translations.text: Get Granny to pass on her craft
Send Kit zooming back to work

"Butterfingers!" Granny scolds, yet her hands never stop, guiding Kit's strip by strip through the curve of a rabbit's ear. At the stroke of midnight a little rabbit lantern sits on the table, its head tilted as if listening. Granny pretends not to smile, then hangs it in the shop window for the whole street to see.

Kit vaults onto his motorbike and hollers back, "Granny! Lantern-moving tomorrow, on me, totally free!" Granny flaps a hand at him. "Off with you, then. Gently on those roads, and no running wild like that rabbit."

Listen well: "Little white rabbit, loves to play, lost its tail and is not afraid." — Guess one character!
It is the character "免"! The rabbit has no tail!
Mooncake! Must be mooncake!

The Lantern Riddle King stroked his beard and laughed: "Wonderful! The rabbit without tail is '免' — this clue is given to you for free: to find the lantern, you must 'wait'. When the moon climbs to the top of the archway, the rabbit will naturally appear."
The Lantern Riddle King laughed until he bent his waist: "Mooncake? You are so hungry your brain has become lotus seed paste! Double yolk lotus seed paste, two eggs — exactly your score!"
{player_name}, do you want to know where the rabbit lantern is? First you must pass my test! If you guess correctly, there is a reward; if you guess wrong... I will laugh louder and louder!
translations.note: 「月」 read as 越 ('the more ... the louder').

translations.text: Listen carefully: "A little white rabbit loves to play; even when it loses its tail, it is not afraid." Guess one Chinese character!

translations.text: The character 'mian'! The rabbit lost its tail!
translations.note: 免 romanised; 47 of 50 characters.

translations.text: A mooncake! It must be a mooncake!

The Riddle King strokes his beard and laughs loudly: "Wonderful! A rabbit without its tail is 'mian', which also means 'free', so I will give you this clue for free: to find the lantern, you must wait. When the moon climbs to the top of the archway, the rabbit will appear by itself."
translations.note: Nested quotation marks converted.

translations.text: The Riddle King laughs so hard that he bends over: "A mooncake? You are so hungry that your brain has turned into lotus paste! A double-yolk lotus paste mooncake has two eggs, which is exactly your score!"
{player_name}! So you want to find the rabbit lantern? You'll have to get past me first! Guess right and win a prize; guess wrong and I'll laugh more and more... moonly!
translations.note: Tried to keep a moon pun.

translations.text: Listen closely: "A little white bunny loves to play; lose its tail and it doesn't mind a bit." What word is left?
translations.note: Recreated as an English word riddle: bunny minus its tail.

translations.text: Bun! Take the tail off 'bunny'!
translations.note: Answer matches the English riddle.

translations.text: Mooncake! Definitely a mooncake!

The Riddle King strokes his beard and roars with laughter. "Brilliant! A bunny without its tail is a bun, and this clue comes free with your bun: to find the lantern, you must wait. When the moon climbs over the archway, the rabbit will show itself."
translations.note: 'Free' follows from the bun answer.

translations.text: The Riddle King doubles over with laughter. "A mooncake? You're so hungry your brain has turned to lotus paste! Double yolk, two eggs... just like your score!"
Halt, {player_name}! Seeking the rabbit lantern, hmm? None shall pass without besting the Riddle King! Guess right and riches await. Guess wrong, and I shall laugh until I'm positively lunar-tic!
translations.note: 'Lunar-tic' recreates the moon pun.

translations.text: Hark, a riddle! "A frisky white bunny lost its tail at play; now it's something you'd eat with your tea today." What word remains?
translations.note: New English riddle; answer: bun.

translations.text: A bun! Bunny, tail snipped. Easy-peasy!
Mooncake!! It's mooncake, I'd bet my lunch!

The Riddle King strokes his beard and booms with laughter. "Bravo! Bunny minus tail equals bun, and tonight buns come free, so here's a free clue to go with it. Lanterns light up for those who wait: when the moon climbs over the archway, the rabbit will appear, and so will a certain delivery boy."
translations.note: Light / wait wordplay for 燈 / 等.

translations.text: The Riddle King collapses in a fit of giggles. "A MOONCAKE? Your brain's gone full lotus paste! Double yolk? Double duck! That's two big fat zeros, my hungry friend, cracked straight onto your scorecard!"
translations.note: British cricket 'duck' = zero.

findings.suggestion: Hear me well: "A little white bunny loves to run and play; snip off its tail and it's lunch for the day!" Now, what word is left?
